html:
The Permanent Settlement of 1793 was the East India Company's deal with the landholders of Bengal. It fixed the land tax for ever and made the tax collectors into landowners. It shaped the countryside of eastern India for 150 years.

Under the Mughals the zamindars had collected the land tax from the villages and kept a share. They did not own the land. After 1765 the Company took over the tax and tried auctioning the right to collect it. This ruined collectors and farmers alike and deepened the famine of 1770.

The governor-general Cornwallis wanted a class of improving landlords like England's. Under his rules:

  • the zamindar became the owner of his estate, free to sell or pass it on;
  • he paid the state a fixed sum each year, never to rise;
  • if he was late by a day, the estate was sold at auction.

Many old families lost their lands within twenty years. Calcutta merchants and officials bought in, and few improved anything. The farmers lost their customary rights and became tenants who could be squeezed. As prices rose, the fixed tax became a bargain for landlords and a loss for the state.

Elsewhere the British taxed the farmer directly. The system was abolished in the 1950s.
sum: The Permanent Settlement of 1793 was the East India Company's deal with the landholders of Bengal. It fixed the land tax for ever and made the tax collectors into landowners. It shaped the countryside of eastern India for 150 years.
